text: La elevada incertidumbre en los tipos de interés está teniendo un impacto notable en los flujos hacia los fondos de crédito. Vía BofA

El software, en particular, sigue mostrando un giro bastante significativo en el sentimiento. Los hedge funds han realizado compras netas de software estadounidense durante cuatro semanas consecutivas y en seis de las últimas ocho, con algunas señales iniciales de un aumento de las compras en posiciones largas. La asignación neta se ha recuperado hasta representar el 5% del valor de mercado neto total en EE. UU., frente al mínimo histórico del 1,3% en febrero, aunque todavía por debajo del 7% de comienzos de año. Esto sitúa el posicionamiento en el percentil 66 frente al último año, pero todavía únicamente en el percentil 13 frente a los últimos cinco años.

Updated $ANT w/ 3Q figures. Some changes: - Nailed the 3Q Revenue figure (came in within 0.1%). Year over year growth mind blowing but sequentially the slowdown is notable - Compute & Infra expense as % of Net Revenues jumps to 58% (from 48% in 2Q). Personnel expenses, sales & marketing is down to offset this, but pretty big jump in my opinion given Revenues slowed down sequentially - On the above, implied 3Q R&D expense (~$9.5B) was basically equal to what they spent through 1Q & 2Q (~$9.7B), and higher than the annual R&D expense from all the previous years (for ex/ 2025 total R&D expense ~$6.3B). Rumor is Fable 5.5 is dropping soon, and is supposedly mindblowingly good. I bet the model drops soon and everyone will stop scrutinizing their numbers and focus shifts to how good the model is / how far ahead they are in the frontier race - $1.96B "non-cash charitable contributions" expense drives most of their "adjustments" in 3Q. One of the benefits of working at Anthropic is they match their employees' charitable contributions, which I never modeled as a recurring expense given it was $0 in 2Q, and I've left it out in the forecasts (which is why 4Q margins nosedive) for now - They disclose $895.4B in commitments, but from their per Company disclosure and other ancillary filings I get to $695.3B, weighted avg. over 7 years. A lot of these are "minimum spend" so that plus other undisclosed stuff is what probably bridges to the $895.4B - On the above, Google's commitment rose +$6.8B between S-1 filings, others stayed the same

Las recompras de acciones de las empresas hiperescaladoras alcanzaron un máximo de aproximadamente 45.000 millones de dólares en un solo trimestre a finales de 2021, y llegaron a los 105.000 millones de dólares en todo 2024. Este año suman 7.000 millones de dólares, o un ritmo anualizado de 14.000 millones de dólares.
